conflicts.permit: RBL also automatically receives and tracks certain data about your mobile device (such as your device-type, installed software and language preference) or desktop interface; and may create a unique device or user ID for you.
conflicts.prohibit: RBL does not collect any personally identifiable information or audio/video/image/contact files from your mobile device.
conflicts.situation: A user plays Ultimate Rummy with the RBL SDK, which tracks device data, creates a unique device or user ID, and may detect GPS location.
conflicts.reason: The policy lists device identification number and user identification number as personal information, yet states RBL collects no personally identifiable information. It does not say whether its definitions apply to RBL.

conflicts.permit: The SDK is integrated with this app for the purposes of profiling the device on media consumption and other device data and utilizing the same to target relevant content and ads to the device
conflicts.prohibit: We restrict access of your Information to our employees, partners, service providers, affiliates, tracking utility companies, contractors and agents and only allow access to those who need to know that information and only in order to process it on our behalf.
conflicts.situation: The RBL SDK in the app profiles the device's media consumption and device data to target content and ads under RBL's own terms.
conflicts.reason: The policy limits partners and tracking companies to processing Information on U Games' behalf, but RBL profiles devices under its own terms of use. The policy does not reconcile the two.

conflicts.permit: Your Information may be archived by us for future reference.
conflicts.prohibit: U Games shall retain the information provided by the users for such period of time as is required to fulfil the purposes for which such information is collected, as outlined in this Privacy Policy, subject to such longer time periods of retention as may be required under any applicable laws.
conflicts.situation: A user's Information has served the purposes for which it was collected, and no law requires longer retention.
conflicts.reason: Archiving for future reference has no stated limit, while the retention clause ties retention to collection purposes or legal requirements. The policy does not say whether archiving is one of those purposes.

conflicts.permit: The third party services we use are listed below may use Cookies to identify Users or they may use the behavioral retargeting techniques, i.e. displaying messages tailored to the User’s interests and behavior, including those detected outside this Application.
conflicts.prohibit: Our contracts with these companies prohibit them from (1) using data collected from our websites or apps for behavioral advertising and (2) sharing data collected from our websites or apps with third parties.
conflicts.situation: A child or parent uses the app, where Google Analytics and Firebase collect data that could support behavioral retargeting.
conflicts.reason: Google Analytics and Firebase are said to be contractually barred from behavioral advertising with website or app data, and are also listed as services that may use behavioral retargeting. The policy does not reconcile the two.

conflicts.permit: The third party services we use are listed below may use Cookies to identify Users or they may use the behavioral retargeting techniques, i.e. displaying messages tailored to the User’s interests and behavior, including those detected outside this Application.
conflicts.prohibit: These cookies do not collect personal data.
conflicts.situation: A visitor uses the website, where Google Analytics sets analytical or performance cookies.
conflicts.reason: Analytical cookies, including those from Google Analytics, are said to collect no personal data, while the listed services, including Google Analytics, may use cookies to identify users. No statement says which governs.

conflicts.permit: These log files are generally retained for a brief period of time, except in cases where they are used for site safety and security, to improve site functionality, or we are legally obligated to retain them for longer time periods.
conflicts.prohibit: If a NatWest Rooster Money family account becomes inactive, data will be retained for no longer than 2 years from the date of last activity, except where we are legally obliged to do so.
conflicts.situation: A family account has been inactive for over two years, and its log files are kept to improve site functionality without any legal obligation.
conflicts.reason: The inactive-account limit allows retention beyond two years only under legal obligation, while the log-file exception for site functionality has no time limit. The policy does not say which governs.

conflicts.permit: You must be at least 13 years old to use the Services.
conflicts.prohibit: We do not knowingly collect any Personal Information from any person who is under the age of 16 or allow them to register an account.
conflicts.situation: A 14-year-old with parental permission creates a User Profile through Facebook, which supplies a birthday, so Haystack learns the user's age.
conflicts.reason: The Terms of Use, which include the Privacy Policy, set the minimum age at 13, while the Privacy Policy bars users under 16 and their data. Neither states which age rule governs.

conflicts.prohibit: Protected classification characteristics under California or federal law.
conflicts.situation: A user connects a Facebook account, and Haystack receives the user's gender and birthday.
conflicts.reason: Sex and age are protected classifications under California and federal law. The California notice marks this category as None and not collected, while the third-party platform list includes gender and birthday.
